quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: It is easier to judge distances at night than during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it hard to see.
Use only one lane position.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use your high beam headlight when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position to handle changing road conditions.

questions.question: What should a helmet do to give you the best protection?

options.text: Have a few cracks.
Not be certified.
Have frayed straps.
Fit snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no damage. Avoid helmets with cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, keeps you away from road hazards, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: What should a face shield do?

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Be so tight that glasses cannot fit underneath it.
Not fasten too tightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield has no scratches, cannot be penetrated, gives clear views to both sides, fastens securely, allows air to pass through, and leaves room for glasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should you ride to stay close while keeping safe distance?

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider safe spacing. Use a single-file line when going around curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you practice this habit now, you will use both brakes correctly during a quick stop.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding which ones are most dangerous.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping a safe distance around your bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: Stay alert and ready to react to hazards. Spot hazards and prioritize which ones need your attention first. Always use your headlight to be more visible and keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Make sudden movements.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you travel?

options.text: Slower than you would during the day under similar conditions.
At the same speed as during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under similar conditions.
On the road shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day in the same weather and traffic. Darkness makes it harder to see hazards, so slowing down helps you avoid them.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: It provides less than half of your motorcycle's braking power.
It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's braking power.
Use it only on wet roads.
It should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: A passenger should never:

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle. They should always lean with the operator during turns. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.
Ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles. This makes them hard to see. Ride defensively and assume others on the road do not see you.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually on the left handgrip.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never touch the operator.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Hold onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Drivers entering a highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. You should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it, if needed.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway from an entrance ramp. Move to a lane away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make room for them to enter safely.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the back of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride toward the front, just behind the leader. More experienced riders behind them can watch them.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. Brake slowly on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Brake immediately.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. It will make the motorcycle less stable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Ride in a staggered line.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered line is usually best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of the following are important, except:

options.text: The helmet meets DOT standards.
The helmet looks nice.
The helmet fits snugly.
The helmet has no defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no damage, such as cracks, loose padding, or torn straps. How the helmet looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Will never need to be replaced.
Will scratch and become brittle over time and need regular replacement.
Should be made of breakable materials so they break away during a crash.
Should not let air pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will scratch and become brittle over time and need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. They will scratch and become brittle as they age. Replace them regularly to stay safe and comfortable.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You cannot see over a load that is too high.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load on a motorcycle raises the center of gravity and makes the bike harder to balance.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to pass quickly.
Not weave between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Riding between slow or parked cars is dangerous. Car doors may open or cars may pull into traffic without warning. You will not have room to move safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers do not expect you there.

questions.question: How can you discourage another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stop other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Weave between portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver move back into your lane too soon.
